newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil ease on arb threat.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil ease on arb threat.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps eased slightly at midday on Monday despite strong physical support on fears of a new wave of arbitrage exports from the Mediterranean and the Black Sea to East Asia, traders said.
"The market is down slightly this morning because there are some concerns over recent reports of arbitrage exports from the Med," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.20/$25.30 per barrel while July was at $25.00/$25.10, both down five cents from Friday's quotes, brokers said.
Brokers said June traded earlier in the day at $25.25.

The lower prices came despite strong physical support on Friday where a Japanese trader bought two 150,000-barrel cargoes at $25.30 and $25.40 per barrel for June 14-18 and June 25-29, respecitvely, free-on-board Singapore basis.
The trades were 50 and 10 cents respectively over Thursday's deals.
Traders said the market shrugged off the support because of talks that ample gas oil cargoes are poised to hit the local market in July from the West.
Some industry sources estimate that four tankers have been fixed for shipment from the Black Sea and Mediterranean, with others estimating as many as seven to eight tankers due for arrival in July.

The weaker prices also come close on the heels of the latest bullish news--India's decision to buy 855,000 tonnes of diesel for delivery in July against initial expectations of between 400,000 and 600,000 tonnes.

The large award came as a much needed boost for the market which had over the past month suffered from poor enduser demand with India importing only 315,000 tonnes in June and China reducing imports for May and June to under 500,000 tonnes a month due to high stocks and port congestion.
The fuel oil market fell at midday after strong sell pressure on the physical market where a 20,000-tonne cargo traded at $101.50 per tonne, down more than a dollar from the previous deal.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $100.25/$101.25, down about 75 cents from Friday.
